question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F={y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,i+x\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j.$ 
Evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(\pi ,1).$
question.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
\text{div}\,F=∇\cdot F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡y) \\  & =2{y}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{x}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(\pi ,1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\cdot F)(\pi ,1) & =2(1)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )+\frac{\pi }{1} \\  & =2(1)(1)+\pi  \\  & =2+\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
